text:
Assistant B is better, mainly because it answers the factual question correctly. Modern language models are pretrained mostly on unlabeled text, learning by predicting the next word, and labeled data is used later for specific tasks. Assistant B says this. Assistant A instead claims language models are trained on labeled input-output pairs, which misrepresents the core training process and directly answers the user's second question wrongly.

Assistant A is also poorly suited to the stated audience of non-technical customers. It is long and dense with jargon (embeddings, sequence-to-sequence, transformers, fine-tuning), and some of its details are inaccurate or misleading, such as describing preprocessing as removing numbers and symbols. Assistant B is brief and plain-language, though it is thin on depth and could have said more explicitly that the self-supervised approach is the key idea.

[[B]]
